_meta.indication: Indicated to reduce proteinuria in adults with primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) at risk of rapid disease progression, generally UPCR ≥ 1.5 g/g.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, multicenter study; patients randomized 1:1 to sparsentan (400 mg once daily) or irbesartan (300 mg once daily active control).
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with biopsy-proven primary IgAN, eGFR ≥ 30 mL/min/1.73 m2, and total urine protein ≥ 1.0 g/day on a maximized stable dose of RAS inhibitor treatment.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint for accelerated approval: change from baseline (Day 1) in UP/C based on a 24-hour urine sample at Week 36.
pivotal_trials.n: 406 total randomized; interim analysis set 141 sparsentan and 140 irbesartan.
pivotal_trials.result: Geometric mean ratio of UP/C at Week 36 relative to baseline was 0.65 (95% CI 0.55, 0.77), i.e., 35% lower (95% CI 23% to 45% lower) for sparsentan vs irbesartan; p<0.0001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%): peripheral edema (14% vs 9% irbesartan), hypotension (14% vs 6%), dizziness (13% vs 5%), hyperkalemia (13% vs 10%), and anemia (5% vs 2%). Serious risks include hepatotoxicity and embryo-fetal toxicity.
target_moa: Sparsentan is a single molecule that is a high-affinity antagonist of both the endothelin type A receptor (ETA R) and the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1 R); antagonizing both receptors reduces proteinuria.
modality: Small molecule (single-molecule dual endothelin and angiotensin II receptor antagonist).

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for HEPATOTOXICITY and EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY; because of these risks FILSPARI is available only through the FILSPARI REMS.

rems.type: FILSPARI is available only through a restricted distribution program (FILSPARI REMS) to mitigate the risks of hepatotoxicity and embryo-fetal toxicity; prescribers, patients, and pharmacies must enroll.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee Meeting was held for this application, as it did not raise significant or controversial issues meriting outside expertise and due to concerns about impacting the integrity of the ongoing study.

description.text: Converted accelerated approval to full approval to slow kidney function decline in adults with primary IgA nephropathy at risk for disease progression

citations.quote: We approved this NDA under the regulations at 21 CFR 314 Subpart H for accelerated approval of new drugs for serious or life-threatening illnesses. Approval of this supplement fulfills your commitments made under 21 CFR 314.510.

description.text: Changed liver monitoring frequency to every 3 months with corresponding labeling and REMS modifications (not a new indication)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for a change to the frequency of the liver monitoring and corresponding changes to the approved labeling and proposed modifications to the approved Filspari risk evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS). This supplement is, in part, in response to our March 11, 2025 REMS Modification Notification letter.

description.text: Added a new indication to reduce proteinuria in adult and pediatric patients aged 8 years and older with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) without nephrotic syndrome

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the addition of a new indication for Filspari (sparsentan) to reduce proteinuria in adult and pediatric patients aged 8 years and older with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) without nephrotic syndrome, and proposed modifications to the approved Filspari REMS.

surrogate_endpoint.text: A substantial reduction in proteinuria (change from baseline in UP/C at Week 36), accepted as a reasonably likely surrogate endpoint for disease progression in IgAN.

citations.quote: Given the available data, the Division of Cardiology and Nephrology (the Division) accepts a substantial reduction in proteinuria as a reasonably likely surrogate endpoint in IgA nephropathy and as a basis for accelerated approval.
The primary efficacy endpoint for the interim analysis was the change from baseline (Day 1) in the UP/C based on a 24-hour urine sample at Week 36 (i.e., endpoint for accelerated approval).

This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on a reduction of proteinuria. It has not been established whether Filspari slows kidney function decline in patients with IgAN. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory clinical trial.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Conduct a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (PMR 4330-1) to describe and verify the clinical benefit of sparsentan in IgA nephropathy; the confirmatory endpoint is the rate of change in eGFR over a 110-week period.

citations.quote: 4330-1 Conduct a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to describe and verify the clinical benefit of sparsentan for the treatment of IgA nephropathy. The trial should be adequately powered and of sufficient duration to detect a treatment effect on the endpoint that will be used to describe and verify the clinical benefit.
Confirmatory endpoint	The Division agreed to a confirmatory endpoint based on rate of change in eGFR over a 110-week (approximately 2-year) period

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug status granted 1/11/2021 (Designation Request No. 2017-6144); because of orphan designation the drug is exempt from PREA pediatric assessment.
